newsitem.title: CHINA: China approves new copper mine in northwest.
newsitem.headline: China approves new copper mine in northwest.

text.p: China's State Planning Commission has approved a new copper mine project in northwestern Qinghai province, an official said on Monday.

The Saishitang copper mine, with proven copper reserves of 230,000 tonnes, would have total investment of 230 million yuan ($27.7 million), the official of the Qinghai heavy industry department said from the provincial capital, Xining.
The project, approved last week, was expected to start operation by 2000, he said.
The project would be run by the newly formed Western China Mineral Development Co, set up by the China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Co, he said.
The new firm planned to seek central government approval for another copper mine project, the the Yulong copper mine in Qamdo in the western Tibet region, he said.

The Yulong copper mine, with proven copper reserves of 6.0 million tonnes, would also receive some investment from the Tibet regional government, he said without giving further details. --Beijing Newsroom (8610) 6532-1921
